title: Best Portable Power Stations UK
short: Portable power stations compared by battery capacity, output and charge speed, for camping, off-grid living and home power cuts.
intro: A portable power station's real test is how it performs when the power actually goes out, not just its spec sheet. This guide compares power stations TechRadar tested hands-on across over 50 units, simulating power outages and using them in the field for camping, work and home backup.

products.name: Delta 3 Plus
products.best_for: Most people who want a versatile all-rounder with genuine UPS backup
products.key_spec: 1024Wh capacity, 2400W output, 10ms UPS switchover, expandable to 5kWh
products.summary: TechRadar's top pick, combining high capacity and fast charging with a comprehensive port selection. Its rapid 10ms UPS switchover kept a router, laptop and lights running through simulated power outages with no interruption, though the price is high and accessories are limited.
pros: Expandable up to 5kWh with extra batteries

products.name: Elite 30 V2
products.best_for: Buyers who want an affordable, genuinely portable everyday unit
products.key_spec: 288Wh capacity, 600W output (1500W Lifting Mode), 9.8 x 7 x 6.6in
products.summary: TechRadar found this the 'everyday essential', small enough to sling in a car boot for work or short camping trips, with power output that impressed for such a mini unit. It handled recharging devices and tools during storm-caused outages on a real installation job, though it lacks a built-in light and isn't the largest battery.

products.name: Solix F3800
products.badge: Best for home backup and RVs
products.best_for: Buyers who want to power a whole home or RV, not just devices
products.key_spec: 3840Wh capacity, 6000W output, expandable to 26.9kWh, wheeled design
products.summary: A genuine powerhouse that TechRadar ran a router, space heaters, lights and laptop charging on without issue, with Anker claiming it can even directly charge an EV. Excellent port selection includes UPS AC sockets, NEMA outlets and dual solar inputs, though its size, weight and price mean it's only for those who need serious capacity.
pros: High power output for home and RV use

products.name: Explorer 1000 V2
products.best_for: Campers who want mains-equivalent power with solar charging
products.summary: TechRadar found this easily kept up charging three computers, a camera, drone and lighting for a full day, with a MacBook Pro staying charged on a near-continuous 100W draw for six hours. UPS switchover proved seamless when simulating an outage with a 3D printer, though at 10kg it's a bit heavy and not weatherproofed.

products.name: AC180T
products.best_for: Road-trippers and travellers who can't wait around for a recharge
products.key_spec: 2x 716Wh swappable batteries, 1800W output, integrated Multi-Cooler system
products.summary: Part of Bluetti's SwapSolar series, this doubles as a portable cooler and ice-maker, with hot-swappable batteries that TechRadar found genuinely useful when one runs low. Performance impressed both as a power station and cooler on a real cabin trip, though it's fairly heavy and ports are somewhat limited.
pros: Doubles as a Multi-Cooler with ice-maker

products.name: Pioneer Na
products.best_for: Buyers who need reliable power in extremely cold conditions
products.key_spec: 900Wh capacity, sodium-ion battery, charges to -15°C, discharges to -25°C
products.summary: The world's first sodium-ion portable power station, giving superior thermal stability in cold weather compared to lithium units. TechRadar's team found it easily handled a laptop, small fridge and LED lighting simultaneously, with tactile buttons usable while wearing gloves, though capacity is modest for the price and it's fairly heavy.
pros: Sodium-ion works better in cold weather
cons: Relatively low 900Wh capacity for the price

products.name: Power 1000 Mini
products.badge: Best for drone operators and creators
products.best_for: Content creators and drone operators who need power on the move
products.key_spec: 1008Wh capacity, 800W output, SDC port for DJI drones, built-in retractable USB-C cable
products.summary: Surprisingly portable for a 1kWh-class unit, TechRadar noted the built-in retractable USB-C cable as a standout touch, ensuring you can always charge a device even without spare cables. The SDC port recharges DJI drones directly, though output is limited compared to full-size stations and solar accessories feel behind competitors.
cons: Limited output vs full-size power stations

guide.q: What capacity do I actually need?
guide.a: For charging phones, laptops and small devices while camping, 300-1000Wh is usually plenty, like the Bluetti Elite 30 or Jackery Explorer here. For home backup during power cuts, running things like a fridge, router and lighting, look at 1000Wh or above; for whole-home or RV backup, a unit like the Anker Solix F3800 with several kWh of capacity is more appropriate.

guide.q: What does UPS switchover time mean, and why does it matter?
guide.a: UPS (uninterruptible power supply) mode lets a power station instantly take over if mains power cuts out, and the switchover time is how long that handover takes. A fast switchover, like the 10ms on the EcoFlow Delta 3 Plus or DJI Power 1000 Mini here, means sensitive electronics like routers or computers won't drop out or reboot during a power cut.

Solar charging is genuinely useful for extended off-grid trips or as a backup during long power outages, letting you top up without mains electricity. Check the solar input wattage matches any panels you're considering, since a mismatch will slow charging significantly.

Most portable power stations use lithium (specifically LFP) batteries, which perform well in most conditions and are widely available. Sodium-ion, like the Bluetti Pioneer Na here, is a newer technology that specifically handles extreme cold better, worth considering only if you regularly need power in sub-zero conditions.
